title: Lockstep CUDA-Graph Resilience and Stream Fallbacks for Stable Multi-Stream Decode
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Problem: We observe non-deterministic CUDA graph capture failures and silent token mis-ordering during multi-stream decode when kernels with different workspace or algorithm choices are selected between prefill and decode phases. This ticket scopes a focused engineering effort to make graph capture/resume deterministic across stream groups, add safe fallbacks when replay fails, and align kernel-selection heuristics with KV-cache and attention tiling to preserve correctness and latency SLOs.

Goals: 
- Make CUDA graph capture deterministic across concurrent streams for common model shapes (up to 8 streams per GPU).
- Ensure replay correctness: identical outputs for captured+replayed paths vs. non-captured baseline within floating-point tolerance and no token reordering regressions.
- Implement safe automatic fallback to prefill-on-decode (or synchronous execution) on rare capture mismatch without dropping requests.
- Improve kernel selection logic to consider prefill/decode clustering, attention tiling layouts, and workspace constraints to reduce capture churn.

Scope & Non-goals: 
- Includes changes in runtime kernel heuristics, capture orchestration, and a small scheduler to group compatible captures.
- Does NOT include a full rewrite of the kernel library or large model architecture changes. Quantization-specific regressions are out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.

Design summary: 
1) Capture lockstep groups: group concurrent streams into "capture classes" based on sequence length bucket, model config hash (attention layout + KV cache stride), and kernel capability mask. Capture will be attempted only within a class to avoid graph mismatch.
2) Deterministic recapture policy: introduce a versioned capture fingerprint (kernel IDs + parameter sizes + allocator signature) recorded at capture time; on replay mismatch, attempt a deterministic recapture path up to N times with exponential backoff, then run the fallback.
3) Kernel selection rules: prefer attention kernels that are stable across prefill->decode boundaries. Add a penalty for kernels that require per-request workspace that differs by sequence-length. Use a small ML-informed heuristic table (learned from telemetry offline) to pick stable kernel variants when cost delta is within X%.
4) Safe fallback: if replay fails or recapture repeatedly mismatches, transparently route affected requests to synchronous decode with the most compatible kernel and record detailed diagnostics. No request should be dropped; SLAs prefer slightly higher latency over errors.
5) Testing harness: expand the GPU unit test runner to simulate concurrent captures with synthetic interleaving and replay mismatches. Add end-to-end checks comparing token-by-token outputs for baseline vs captured+replayed paths within configurable tolerance.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Capture stability metric (failures per 10k captures) reduced by >= 90% for top-10 models in catalog under multi-stream load.
- No observable token-order regressions in 99.99th percentile of synthetic test runs.
- Automatic fallback triggers create a <0.5% request tail increase in latency under normal load, and zero silent errors.
- Instrumentation exposable in console: capture_fails, recapture_attempts, fallback_routes, and kernel_selection_decision per capture class.

Rollout plan: 
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 experimental flag. Canary on 2 dedicated GPU hosts with replay logging enabled.
- Week 1: dry-run only telemetry collection (no fallback triggered).
- Week 2: enable recapture attempts and controlled fallback at 0.1% sampling.
- Week 3: enable global fallback with metrics guardrails and automated rollback if capture_fails spike > 2x baseline.

Metrics to monitor: capture_fail_rate, recapture_success_rate, fallback_rate, end-to-end latency p99, token_consistency_check_fail_count.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Increased latency due to conservative kernel selection. Mitigation: ML heuristic with cost delta threshold; gradual rollout and A/B tests.
- Risk: Unhandled edge-case model layouts. Mitigation: whitelist-by-model and quick disable via feature flag; add model onboarding checklist.

- Test harness PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Telemetry dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capture-stability
